blind_comparisons.question: Which pitch(t) series is a camera whose clamp is applied during integration rather than after it?
blind_comparisons.blind_rationale: Both series ramp monotonically to a bound and then hold a single bit-exact value for the rest of the window, with zero frames past the bound and zero frames returning towards zero. The discriminator the item names — a frame at -55.3 that shows the clamp being applied after integration — does not occur in either series, so there is nothing left to choose between them on this question.

Any pack built from it is trivially identifiable by the absence of noise, so the comparison cannot be fair. Round 1 hit the same wall from the other direction and mis-identified the zero-residual series as synthetic.

biggest_gap.what: The save does not carry enemies[].prev_state. RI-JRN05 M5 run as written — identical 120-frame pre-roll on both sides, identical 600-frame script, seed 4711, control vs loaded — gives control body_sha256 5d0830f9b9e3ea71… and loaded d52edb76370c7c08…, differing on 219 of 600 frames in exactly that field: control "IDLE", loaded null, from frame 0 onward. The serialised entity record carries state, anim_frame, anim_phase0 and state_entered_ago_frames and stops there. world.entities is a durable path in game/data/save-manifest.json and prev_state is on no volatile list, so manifest rule V1 makes it a defect by the manifest's own terms. The same probe against round-1 commit 8714e38 reproduces it exactly, so it is pre-existing and was missed by both the build and the previous verdict, which recorded M5 as passing.
biggest_gap.why_it_matters: A player who reloads gets an enemy whose state history has been erased, so the first transition after a reload is taken from a different predecessor than the one the unsaved game would have used — RI-JRN05's own "how we lose" #5: nothing a player does catches it until a boss behaves differently after a reload.

remedy.action: Serialise prev_state in the entity record next to state and state_entered_ago_frames and restore it in the load path; add prev_state to the World group field list in game/data/save-manifest.json so RI-JRN05 M4's two-directional set-difference covers it; and extend the R9 rung and RI-JRN05 M5 to compare the full field set of the control and loaded traces rather than only body_sha256 of a window, printing the differing field names — round 1's M5 run passed precisely because it did not.
remedy.acceptance: Re-run RI-JRN05 M5 (or corpus/90-verdicts/wave1/artifacts/W1-00-r2/p10-m5.mjs) at seed 4711 and at one other seed: the control and loaded traces must have identical body_sha256 after re-basing the absolute frame indices, and the field-level diff must be EMPTY. Today it is {"enemies[].prev_state": 219} of 600 frames.

secondary_observations.what: The seed reaches exactly one field. rng.draws reaches 1 and stays there over 3,600 frames, and the only differing simulation field across four critic-chosen seed pairs is enemies[].anim_frame. On mth-warmup-noenemy — same world, same script, no entity — seeds 90210 and 8675309 give 0 of 1,800 frames differing outside .rng.seed and max(rng.draws) = 0. HARNESS.md §8 D6 says setSeed() is honoured for world generation and content selection so a seed change visibly changes the run; today it is not.

tools/platform/alloc-probe.mjs reports max(0, slope): its own line reads "9828 B @ 120000 steps - 10344 B @ 60000 steps = 0 B". It prints FAIL for F1/F5 at --steps 20000 and PASS at --steps 60000 on the same tree.

The same tool's self-test measures escaping literals (29.13 B each), which the CDP defaults already report correctly, so it would pass with the flag it exists to verify turned off. The case that needs the flag is dying literals: 0.073 B vs 9.16 B per literal in my run.
queueInputs({f: 0}) — a frame with no action key at all — still returns 1 and does nothing. Unrecognised keys (tap, wibble) now throw correctly, but the no-key case was not covered by the fix.
getBuildInfo().commit and .builtAt are still both null (RI-MTH01 A03).
camera({pos: [1, 2]}) still returns {pos: [1, 2, null], …} rather than throwing.

getStorageInfo() returns {} until a save has been written in the session, so RI-JRN05 M10's backend === indexeddb cannot be attested from a cold read. After a write, localStorage holds exactly one record, elder-souls.pointer, 63 bytes against a 1024-byte budget.

The camera height residual over 900 frames of a sprint is identically zero — one distinct value 1.4515, roll_deg 0 and camera.shake [0,0] on every frame. RI-CAM06 §E's 0.004 m bar is met by having no vertical camera behaviour rather than by damping one.

gap_closure.measured_value: 100.000% of 3600 frames differ outside .rng.seed on four critic-chosen seed pairs; max(rng.draws) = 1 in both runs of every pair
gap_closure.acceptance_restated: Re-run trace.mjs --scenario cmb-duel-infantry at two seeds and diff field-by-field: max(rng.draws) > 0 in both runs, and >= 5% of frames differ in at least one field other than .rng.seed.
gap_closure.note: Closed on its own acceptance string, re-measured with seeds the builder did not choose (90210/8675309, 271828/999983, 1/2147483647, 90210/1), against round 1's measured 0.0%. The discriminator was separately shown to have teeth: on mth-warmup-noenemy the same seeds give 0.0% and max(rng.draws) = 0. The residual — that the seed reaches only enemies[].anim_frame — is recorded as a secondary observation, not as a reason to withhold closure. tools/gap-ledger.mjs IGNORES this closure because it is in the same wave (1) that opened the gap, and I am leaving it rejected rather than writing wave: 2 to make it stick — the measurement is on the record with its artifacts for the wave-2 critic on this path to adopt. That a remediation round inside a wave cannot retire a gap it genuinely fixed is itself a process gap, recorded here.

arbitration_questions.question: Is a save that omits a durable entity field, where the omission produces a post-load trace divergence in a field that no AI currently reads, a triggered hard fail or a deferred defect?
arbitration_questions.souls_side: RI-JRN05 HF1 is unconditional — "any post-load trace divergence" — because the whole point of the round trip is that the loaded world is the saved world, and a field that is wrong now is a boss that behaves differently after a reload later.
arbitration_questions.morrowind_side: prev_state is arguably an honest null for a session that has no previous state, and no system in this build reads it, so the divergence has zero observable consequence today.

arbitration_questions.question: sim_units is defined in RI-PLT01 §A in terms of cpu_index_reference for the phone-mid class, and that constant has no numeric value anywhere in the corpus. Until it is declared, M3 (8 points) and RI-PLT03 P6 are unscoreable on every machine including real hardware. Who declares it, and does a dimension nobody can measure keep scoring 0 against the build?
arbitration_questions.souls_side: SCORING.md §1.1 is explicit: unmeasurable is 0, fail-closed, and the build carries the loss regardless of whose fault the hole is.
arbitration_questions.morrowind_side: Charging the build for a constant the corpus never wrote makes the item a permanent 8-point tax on every platform verdict until a phone is attested, which is a corpus debt masquerading as a build score.

arbitration_questions.question: A gap fixed and re-measured inside the same wave, by a critic who did not build the fix, cannot be closed: tools/gap-ledger.mjs requires a LATER wave's critic and ignores the closure. The ledger therefore reports GAP-W1-platform-prng-never-drawn as blocking against a build where it is measurably fixed.
arbitration_questions.souls_side: SCORING.md §5 rule 1 exists so a fix cannot certify itself; loosening it by wave is how closures start being taken by the people who benefit from them.
arbitration_questions.morrowind_side: The rule's stated intent is that closure is a CRITIC act by someone who did not build the fix, which is satisfied here; the wave comparison is a proxy for independence, not the thing itself, and it is now producing a false open gap.

arbitration_questions.question: verdict.schema.json has additionalProperties: false and no ar3 field, while the critic charter requires AR-3 (seam sterility) to be recorded in every verdict. Round 1 carried it in notes and so does this verdict.
arbitration_questions.souls_side: The schema is the contract and a verdict that adds a field is invalid.
arbitration_questions.morrowind_side: A mandatory check with no home in the machine-readable artifact is a check that nothing can aggregate, which is the false-enforcement pattern BAR-CRITIQUE-02 named.

notes: AR-3 (seam sterility, ARBITRATION.md §3): seam_sterile = TRUE, carried here because verdict.schema.json has no ar3 field. This piece is the measurement seam itself — a fixed-step loop, a trace format, an input pipeline and a save blob — and carries no boundary-crossing interaction by design. Round 1 recorded the one place it bears on the seam: with rng.draws == 0 nothing that is supposed to vary could be shown to vary. That is now half-fixed. The counter moves, but the seed's reach is one animation counter on one class of object: on mth-warmup-noenemy the counter is still 0 and the seed still changes nothing at all (critic2-seed-sensitivity.json). Reported for the RI-CMP01 project-level floor. — Ordering note (CRITIC-DOCTRINE §8): the gap ledger entry for platform.determinism.harness was read only after every raw measurement in §1-§4 had been taken and after both blind results were recorded; its closure in gap_closure rests on trace fields produced before it was read.
